extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners/agents, and patent examiners handling design patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for claiming priority/benefit, expedited examination, term, reissue, and continuation/CIP practice specifically for design patent applications under U.S. law and applicable treaties. Covers timing, form, fees, and examiner actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority — six month filing requirement (35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), 172)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application claiming priority to a foreign application must be filed within six (6) months from the earliest filing date of the foreign application in order to obtain the benefit of that earlier foreign filing date (35 U.S.C. 172).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subsequent U.S. design application is filed more than six months after the foreign filing date, the claim for priority cannot be based on that foreign application unless a petition to restore the right of priority under 37 CFR 1.55(c) is granted. See MPEP § 213-216 for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to restore right of priority (37 CFR 1.55(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the U.S. design application is filed within two months of the expiration of the six‑month period and the delay was unintentional, the right of priority may be restored by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to restore the right of priority must include: (1) the priority claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), 386(a) or (b) in an application data sheet identifying the foreign application (application number, country/authority, day/month/year of filing unless previously submitted); (2) the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m); and (3) a statement that the delay in filing within the six‑month period was unintentional. The petition must be filed in the subsequent application (or earliest nonprovisional claiming benefit). The Director may require additional information. Address: Mail Stop Petition, Commissioner for Patents. Examiner note: insert country name where bracketed in form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design applications may not claim provisional benefit (35 U.S.C. 119(e) / 35 U.S.C. 172)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design applications may not claim the benefit of a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 119(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.55 and MPEP § 213–216 for related formal requirements. Because a design application cannot claim the benefit of a provisional, a design application cannot obtain the provisional filing date via an intermediate utility application that directly claims provisional benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy requirement for foreign priority (37 CFR 1.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of the foreign application is required to support a claim to foreign priority under 37 CFR 1.55.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For design applications, the certified copy must be filed during the pendency of the application unless filed with a petition under 37 CFR 1.55(g) together with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g) and a showing of good and sufficient cause for the delay. If the certified copy is filed after the date the issue fee is paid, the patent will not include the priority claim unless corrected by a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323. Examiner notes indicate where to insert foreign application number, country, and filing date in form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim presentation timing and form (pre/post Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: The form and timing for presenting a claim for foreign priority depend on the filing date of the U.S. application: if the application was filed before September 16, 2012, the priority claim must be made in either the oath or declaration or in an application data sheet; if the application was filed on or after September 16, 2012, the claim for foreign priority must be presented in an application data sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the case of a design application, the claim must be presented during pendency unless filed with a petition under 37 CFR 1.55(e). If the claim is filed after payment of the issue fee, the priority claim will not be included in the patent unless corrected by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323. Use appropriate form paragraphs and insertions as noted in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority to Hague / international design (35 U.S.C. 386(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For design applications filed on or after May 13, 2015, a claim for priority may be made pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 386(a) to an international design application filed under the Geneva Act of the Hague Agreement, provided the international design application designates at least one Contracting Party other than the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The United States recognizes claims for right of priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) based on applications filed under treaties such as the Hague Agreement, Uniform Benelux Act, and European Community Design. Required information when claiming priority under such treaties includes: (A) application number, (B) date of filing, and (C) name and location of the national or inter‑governmental authority which received the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 — specific reference requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim the benefit of an earlier‑filed U.S. application under 35 U.S.C. 120, the later‑filed application must contain a specific reference to the earlier‑filed application (i.e., identify the prior application and relationship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012 the specific reference must be in the application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76). For applications filed prior to Sept 16, 2012, the specific reference must be in the first sentence(s) of the specification or in an application data sheet. The Director may consider failure to submit such an amendment within the required time as a waiver of any benefit; the Director may establish procedures (including payment of fee under section 41(a)(7)) to accept an unintentionally delayed submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior application types eligible for 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior‑filed application must name the inventor or joint inventor named in the later application and must be one of: (i) a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) entitled to a filing date as set forth in §§ 1.53(b) or 1.53(d) with the basic filing fee paid within the pendency; (ii) an international design application entitled to a filing date in accordance with § 1.1023 and designating the United States; or (iii) an international application entitled to a filing date in accordance with PCT Article 11 and designating the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.78(d) for details. These are the acceptable categories of earlier applications for claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 in design prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely submit reference is waiver of benefit (37 CFR 1.78(d)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in 37 CFR 1.78(e), the failure to timely submit the reference required under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78 in a design application during its pendency is considered a waiver of any benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c) or 386(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a waiver occurs, applicant may be required to change the relationship of the continuing application (e.g., to continuation‑in‑part) or delete the benefit claim. For post‑Sept 16, 2012 filings, applicant can delete or change the benefit claim by filing a corrected ADS in compliance with 37 CFR 1.76(c); for pre‑Sept 16, 2012 filings, by amending the specification or submitting a supplemental ADS per pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.76(c). See MPEP § 211 for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation and divisional application requirements and examiner responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application (other than a continued prosecution application under 37 CFR 1.53(d)) must include a specific reference to the prior‑filed application in compliance with 37 CFR 1.78 to claim benefit. The prior application must disclose the claimed design in the manner required by 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In all continuation and divisional applications, the examiner must determine whether conditions for priority under 35 U.S.C. 120 have been met. If not met, the examiner should notify applicant, specify reasons why benefit is not allowed, and may require applicant to change the relationship or delete the benefit claim. Form paragraphs (e.g., 2.09, 2.10, 2.10.01, 15.26) may be used followed by a specific explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation‑in‑part (CIP) entitlement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation‑in‑part (CIP) repeats some substantial portion or all of an earlier nonprovisional application and adds matter not disclosed in the earlier application. Only when the claim of the CIP is disclosed in the manner provided by 35 U.S.C. 112(a) in the earlier application will the claim be entitled to the benefit of the earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the filing date of the earlier application is not needed (e.g., no intervening prior art), entitlement to benefit in the CIP will not be considered by the examiner. If the earlier application is fatally defective under 35 U.S.C. 112, a second design application filed as a CIP to supply the deficiency is not entitled to the benefit of the earlier filing date. Use form paragraph 15.74 when notifying applicant that the CIP is not entitled to benefit; use 15.74.01 where the claim is not disclosed in the parent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: When foreign priority in parent affects CIP — foreign app as prior art (pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d)/172)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a CIP claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and the parent also claimed foreign priority, and the CIP is not entitled to benefit of the parent (e.g., insufficient disclosure), the foreign application may qualify as prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d)/172 if the foreign application was filed more than six months before the CIP filing date and matured into a form of patent protection prior to the CIP filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should use charts in MPEP § 1504.02 to determine the status of the foreign application. If the foreign application qualifies as prior art and its design anticipates or renders the CIP claim obvious, the claim should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102/103 using appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 15.74.01 followed by rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d)/103(a)). If the status is unknown, use the C‑I‑P caution form 15.75.01.fti and request applicant to inform the Office of the foreign application's status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination eligibility requirements (37 CFR 1.155)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for expedited examination under 37 CFR 1.155 for a design application, the following requirements must be met: (1) the application must include drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84, or for an international design application that designates the United States, must have been published pursuant to Hague Agreement Article 10(3); (2) the applicant must have conducted a preexamination search; and (3) the applicant must file a request for expedited examination including the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(k) and a statement that a preexamination search was conducted (indicating field of search) together with an information disclosure statement in compliance with 37 CFR 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not examine an application that is not in condition for examination even if a request for expedited examination is filed. The preexamination search can be a foreign patent office search. The statement must indicate the field of search (e.g., U.S. Class/Subclass) and include domestic and foreign patent documents and non‑patent literature. The basic filing fee and expedited fee must be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure, form, and processing for expedited examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for expedited examination should use Form PTO/SB/27 (or include the notation 'REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED EXAMINATION OF A DESIGN APPLICATION (37 CFR 1.155)' and 'Doc Code: ROCKET' on the first page) and must identify the corresponding application number. Mailing address and electronic filing instructions are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests are evaluated by the Director of Technology Center 2900. If granted, the application is dispatched for expedited examination and processing is expedited throughout prosecution including appeal. For international design applications, requests should be filed after publication under Hague Article 10(3). If a request fails to comply with requirements but the application is otherwise complete, applicant will be notified of the deficiency and may submit a renewed request; unless all requirements are timely met the application will await regular turn. The Office encourages electronic filing and provides specific mailing/fax addresses for paper/faxed requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of design patent (PLTIA / 35 U.S.C. 173)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patents resulting from applications filed on or after May 13, 2015 have a 15‑year term from the date of grant; patents issued from design applications filed before May 13, 2015 have a 14‑year term from the date of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change results from the Patent Law Treaties Implementation Act of 2012 (PLTIA) implementing the 1999 Geneva Act of the Hague Agreement; see applicable MPEP section for effective dates and transitional provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue of design patent — drawing corrections and term limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application to correct a design patent drawing must follow the practice and procedure for reissue applications (see MPEP Chapter 1400 and §1457). The term of a design patent may not be extended by reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue applications seeking to correct drawings (canceling views, amending views, or adding new views) follow 37 CFR 1.173(b)(3). All changes to the patent drawing must be explained in detail on a separate sheet accompanying the amendment, and a marked‑up copy of any amended drawing figure with annotations indicating changes (clearly labeled 'Annotated Marked‑up Drawings') should be submitted. A reissue application must be filed with a copy of all drawing views of the design patent regardless of whether certain views are being cancelled or amended.
